_note: Every distinct real string in this repository — catalogue variants, corpus wordings, distractors and evaluation rows — with the form both implementations of the normaliser produce for it. Generated only after verifying that the Python and PHP transforms agree on all of them; a disagreement is a bug, not a case to record.
_why: normalise() exists twice, in Python for the matcher and in PHP for seeding and for Postgres trigram queries. The code calls that duplication dangerous and it is right: text normalised one way at index time and another at query time simply fails to match, and nothing errors. That risk was guarded by 22 hand-written fixtures. These are 3,887 strings people actually wrote, covering every character fold, digit form, punctuation mark and glued-size pattern the corpus contains.
